verdicts.reason: A: the card fills almost the whole canvas, so the confetti brand texture shrinks to a thin strip along the top. The headline sits above the bottle, which changes the original reading order. The logo is a tiny orphan jammed under the CTA, and the fine print is nearly as large as the subhead. B keeps the original structure (confetti and bottle above the card, then headline, copy and CTA), but the logo is crammed into the bottom-left corner, the fine print is too large, the CTA is oversized and the card runs off the canvas edges.

A keeps the original top-to-bottom order with clear hierarchy, but the logo is tiny and jammed into the bottom-left corner, the fine print is too large and the CTA is oversized. B forces a two-column layout into a narrow tall frame. The headline wraps into one or two words per line ('Cold / brew, / bottled / this / morning'), the body text is cramped and the bottle is clipped at the card's left edge. A large dead area also sits above the CTA.

A has the logo jammed into the bottom-left corner, an oversized CTA, a card bleeding off both sides, and fine print as big as the subhead. B uses the same structure with side margins on the card, a better-proportioned CTA and the logo centred under the CTA on a shared axis. It still has flaws: the logo is too small to read, the fine print is oversized and the bottom is slightly cramped.
